name: Portugal
gaps: No independent bird clubs with their own sites were found for mainland districts such as Porto, Algarve or Coimbra, or for Madeira, beyond SPEA's national programmes; a Madeira group using the ornithological name turned out to be a cage bird show organiser and was excluded.

Active public Facebook groups for Portuguese birders (Aves de Portugal, Aves de Portugal Continental 2.0, Aves Silvestres de Portugal) were found but Facebook blocks automated verification, so no unverified Facebook link is included here.

The eBird Portugal portal returns a bot check page to automated requests even though it is the platform SPEA itself recommends for logging sightings, so treat that link as needing a manual sanity check.

name: United Kingdom
gaps: Ceredigion: no independent bird club website was found, birders there coordinate mainly through a Facebook group and WhatsApp chats rather than a public site.
Staffordshire, Warwickshire and Worcestershire: none has its own county bird club, all three share the West Midland Bird Club alongside the West Midlands, listed once under West Midlands.
Northern Ireland Ornithologists Club: its site nioc.co.uk no longer resolves and its Facebook page could not be curl verified, so it has been left out rather than listing a dead link.
Outer Hebrides: outerhebridesbirds.org.uk currently returns a Cloudflare phishing warning on its live domain, so no verified link is listed for this region.
Next Generation Birders: its blog has had no posts since 2016 and its main presence now is an X account that needs login to browse, so it has been left out as likely dormant.
Caithness: the branch's own domain, caithnessbirds.co.uk, did not respond to repeated checks, so the Scottish Ornithologists Club branch page is listed instead.
